analysis.investment_thesis: EPW India's Magic Formula metrics are deeply unattractive — Earnings Yield is ~4.3% (EBIT ₹6 Cr / EV ~₹141 Cr), well below the 6% floor I require. While headline ROCE looks strong, cash flows flatly contradict the accounting profits, disqualifying this from consideration.
key_strengths: Revenue tripled in one year (₹19 Cr → ₹53 Cr), showing real commercial momentum
Zero finance cost historically and asset-light model suits working capital cycles in theory
High promoter holding (71.4%) aligns management with the business
key_risks: Negative FCF of -₹12 Cr in FY25 against net profit of ₹4 Cr — cash earnings are fictional at this point
Borrowings surged from ₹0 to ₹12 Cr in one year to fund working capital; equity base is only ₹5 Cr (2.4x leverage)
Refurbished IT hardware is a commoditized, low-moat business with no pricing power
red_flags: Operating CF of -₹11 Cr in FY25 despite ₹4 Cr net profit — massive working capital bleed
Company is micro-cap (₹129 Cr) with only two years of meaningful revenue history — no track record of sustained ROIC
P/E of 31x on ₹4 Cr profit in a no-moat sector is unjustifiable valuation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT is ₹6 Cr for FY25. EV = Market Cap (₹129 Cr) + Debt (₹12 Cr) ≈ ₹141 Cr, giving an Earnings Yield of ~4.3% — well below my 6% floor and nowhere near the 12–15% range I find attractive. ROCE of 65.7% looks eye-catching, but this is an artifact of a nearly zero equity base two years ago; the denominator is artificially tiny and doesn't reflect a genuine competitive advantage compounding capital.

The cash flow statement exposes the real problem: FY25 shows ₹4 Cr net profit but -₹11 Cr operating cash flow and -₹12 Cr FCF. In a refurbished hardware distribution business, this signals aggressive inventory buildup to support rapid revenue growth — but growth funded entirely by borrowings (₹12 Cr) on a ₹5 Cr equity base is fragile. A single demand slowdown or credit squeeze destroys the equity. The Magic Formula requires genuine earnings, and this business isn't generating them yet on a cash basis.
